spots.summary: Orléans Cathedral is a Roman Catholic cathedral located in the city of Orléans, France. The cathedral is the seat of the Bishop of Orléans.

spots.name: Musée des Beaux-Arts d'Orléans
spots.summary: The Musée des beaux-arts d'Orléans is a museum in the city of Orléans in the Loiret department and the Centre-Val de Loire region in France.

spots.name: Cenabum
spots.summary: Cenabum, Gaul was the name of the capital city of the Carnutes, located near the present French city of Orléans. Cenabum was an oppidum and a thriving commercial town on the Loire river.

spots.name: Hôtel Groslot
spots.summary: The Hôtel Groslot was the City Hall until the 1980s when a modern building across the street replaced it for most civil administration functions. You can still get married in the grand rooms of the Hôtel and some rooms close to visitors during marriage ceremonies. Saint-Aignan d'Orléans

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint-Aignan is a collegiate church in the Bourgogne quarter of Orléans on the north bank of the Loire, France. The church is dedicated to Anianus, a 5th-century bishop of Orléans, who, according to legend, persuaded Attila the Hun not to sack the city.

spots.name: George V Bridge, Orléans
spots.summary: The George V Bridge is a road and tram bridge that crosses the Loire in Orléans, France. It is an arched masonry bridge spanning a distance of 325 m. Designed by Jean Hupeau, it was built between 1751 and 1760, at the request of Daniel-Charles Trudaine, administrator and civil engineer.

spots.name: Neuvy-en-Sullias Hoard
spots.summary: The Neuvy-en-Sullias Hoard is a Gallic and Gallo-Roman group of bronze objects, including sculptures of animals and two groups of statuettes. It was discovered in 1861 in a sand mine in Neuvy-en-Sullias and is now mostly held in the Musée historique et archéologique de l'Orléanais in Orleans.
